title: Music in the market of Daulatabad
body: Ibn Battuta described a market place in Daulatabad for male and female singers, known as Tarababad. He called it one of the greatest and most beautiful bazaars. It had numerous shops, and every shop had a door leading into the house of the owner. The shops were decorated with carpets, and at the centre of a shop there was a swing on which the female singer sat while her attendants swung her. In the middle of the market stood a large carpeted cupola where the chief of the musicians took his place every Thursday after the dawn prayers. The female singers came in successive crowds, sang before him and danced until dusk. There were mosques in the bazaar for offering prayers. One of the Hindu rulers alighted at the cupola every time he passed by, and the singers would sing before him; even some Muslim rulers did the same.
